evidence.title: Taung child — revised Pliocene chronology
evidence.summary: The juvenile type specimen of Australopithecus africanus documents an early southern African branch. A new flowstone and palaeomagnetic analysis proposes this age interval.
evidence.limits: The quarry destroyed the precise recovery context. This new interpretation depends on flowstone association and uranium-system assumptions; it is not direct DNA evidence or proof of interbreeding. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Published approximate age or dating interval; the display uses 1950 minus calendar age for placement. This is not a continuous occupation interval.

evidence.title: Wonderwerk — early cave occupation
evidence.summary: Oldowan artifacts in the cave’s deep deposits establish early hominin use of a sheltered interior.
evidence.limits: Magnetostratigraphy and cosmogenic dating constrain deposition; neither a resident population size nor a specific toolmaker is known. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Published approximate age or dating interval; the display uses 1950 minus calendar age for placement. This is not a continuous occupation interval.

evidence.title: Wonderwerk — earlier fire association
evidence.dateLabel: 1.79–1.07 million years ago · broad stratigraphic bracket
evidence.summary: A 2026 study identifies heated small-mammal bones in an early archaeological layer using luminescence and infrared methods.
evidence.limits: Fire associated with hominins does not establish deliberate ignition, a built hearth or cooking. The wide interval is chronological uncertainty. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Published approximate age or dating interval; the display uses 1950 minus calendar age for placement. This is not a continuous occupation interval.

evidence.title: Wonderwerk — Acheulean fire traces
evidence.summary: Burned bone and plant ash within Acheulean sediments provide evidence of fire inside the cave.
evidence.limits: Microscopic burning evidence is distinct from proof of making fire or a permanently occupied home. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Published approximate age or dating interval; the display uses 1950 minus calendar age for placement. This is not a continuous occupation interval.

evidence.title: Kathu Pan 1 — proposed hafted spear tips
evidence.summary: Wear, damage and experimental comparison support interpreting some stone points as hafted hunting weapons.
evidence.limits: A functional inference from stone tools; preserved wooden spears and diagnostic maker fossils are absent. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Published approximate age or dating interval; the display uses 1950 minus calendar age for placement. This is not a continuous occupation interval.

evidence.title: Kalambo Falls — interlocking worked logs
evidence.summary: Two shaped logs fitted together document large-scale woodworking beside the river.
evidence.limits: Associated sediment ages provide the minimum-age interpretation. The structure’s exact function is unknown; it is not a demonstrated house. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Luminescence age 476 ± 23 ka; displayed at the dated sediment envelope. “At least” is retained: this is not an upper limit on the structure’s age.

evidence.title: Kalambo Falls — younger wooden tools
evidence.summary: A separate dated horizon preserves worked wooden implements, extending the evidence beyond the paired logs.
evidence.limits: This is a distinct sampled phase, not proof of uninterrupted settlement between horizons. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Published approximate age or dating interval; the display uses 1950 minus calendar age for placement. This is not a continuous occupation interval.

evidence.title: Kalambo Falls — later woodworking horizon
evidence.summary: Another wooden-tool horizon records repeated use of the riverine landscape.
evidence.limits: Preservation in waterlogged sediments gives an unusual view of perishable technology; the toolmakers are not securely identified. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Published approximate age or dating interval; the display uses 1950 minus calendar age for placement. This is not a continuous occupation interval.

evidence.title: Kabwe / Broken Hill — dated cranium
evidence.summary: Direct analyses place the Kabwe cranium near the time of early Homo sapiens while retaining a different combination of anatomical traits.
evidence.limits: Taxonomic names such as Homo heidelbergensis and H. rhodesiensis remain debated. Mining destroyed the original cave context. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Published approximate age or dating interval; the display uses 1950 minus calendar age for placement. This is not a continuous occupation interval.

evidence.title: Twin Rivers — pigment and Lupemban archaeology
evidence.dateLabel: Approximately 270–170 thousand years ago · disputed association
evidence.summary: Stone tools and collected pigments document Middle Stone Age activity in limestone cavities.
evidence.limits: This is a published archaeological age interpretation. Complex speleothem associations and redeposition limit confidence; older cave-formation dates do not independently date every artifact. Lupemban is a technological label, not a named people. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Published approximate age or dating interval; the display uses 1950 minus calendar age for placement. This is not a continuous occupation interval.

evidence.title: Mumbwa Caves — basal Middle Stone Age
evidence.summary: Basal archaeological deposits precede several later occupation episodes.
evidence.limits: Shown at a minimum-age anchor, not a known arrival date. Human burials once assigned to this ancient occupation have instead yielded much younger farmer-period dates. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Published lower age limit >170 ka; displayed at its minimum anchor without inventing an older bound.

evidence.title: Mumbwa Caves — interglacial occupation
evidence.summary: A separate Middle Stone Age occupation phase records repeated cave use in central Zambia.
evidence.limits: The archaeological sequence is discontinuous. The range does not identify a single ethnic population or the age of the later burials. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Published approximate age or dating interval; the display uses 1950 minus calendar age for placement. This is not a continuous occupation interval.

evidence.title: Mumbwa Caves — later Pleistocene occupation
evidence.summary: A later occupation horizon adds another dated return to the cave.
evidence.limits: This approximate published phase age is separate from younger Holocene deposits and burials. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Published approximate age or dating interval; the display uses 1950 minus calendar age for placement. This is not a continuous occupation interval.

evidence.title: Florisbad — human remains and competing chronologies
evidence.dateLabel: 259 ± 35 ka ESR; alternative 212–154 ka sediment bracket
evidence.summary: A partial cranium and tooth bear on African Middle Pleistocene human diversity. A 2026 stratigraphic study proposes a younger context than the longstanding tooth ESR age.
evidence.limits: The display spans competing age models, not a continuous occupation or a combined confidence interval. Spring reworking, original provenance and taxonomic attribution remain important limitations. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Display envelope 294–154 ka covers the old tooth ESR uncertainty and newer 212–154 ka context bracket; the two estimates are kept separate in the label.

evidence.title: Likonong — early highland occupation
evidence.summary: Sparse artifacts in basal layer BL3 document an early occupation pulse in Lesotho’s highlands.
evidence.limits: Luminescence ages may be maxima because grains were incompletely bleached; the associated hominin lineage is unknown. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Published approximate age or dating interval; the display uses 1950 minus calendar age for placement. This is not a continuous occupation interval.

evidence.title: Likonong — second early occupation pulse

evidence.dateBasis: Published approximate age or dating interval; the display uses 1950 minus calendar age for placement. This is not a continuous occupation interval.

evidence.title: Likonong — later Middle Stone Age horizons

evidence.title: White Paintings Shelter — Middle Stone Age deposits
evidence.dateLabel: Sediments: 94.3 ± 9.4 and 66.4 ± 6.5 ka; artifact associations disputed
evidence.summary: Stone artifacts document Middle Stone Age activity at Tsodilo in northern Botswana.
evidence.limits: Refits demonstrate substantial vertical and lateral artifact movement. Sediment ages cannot securely date each artifact, and the basal deposits may be older than 100 ka. Wall paintings are not dated by these measurements. Public coordinates are rounded for regional orientation, not an excavation plan.
evidence.dateBasis: Nash et al. (2016), section 2.4, reports these OSL sediment ages. Display bounds cover both quoted uncertainty ranges (103.7–59.9 ka), using 1950 minus age; this is not a single occupation interval.
